- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and continue upward; apply a downward correction of 3–8% in the following 5–7 days.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates when prices are near historical highs, underestimates when near lows; adjust forecast by subtracting 1–3 standard deviations from mean of recent 10-day window.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days; shift forecast horizon backward by 1–2 days for short-term (0–7 day) predictions.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a peak, model fails to correct; apply a “sudden drop” heuristic: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days if true price drops >5% from peak.
- Model underestimates prices during low-volatility periods; increase forecast by 1–3% if recent 30-day average is below 70.00.
